result.title: The Geometry Is the Memory: Task-Density Routing for Continual LoRA
result.summary: Freezing older adapters does not ensure that a continual learner will select and use them properly at inference time. When multiple adapters exist, routing among them and identifying the adapter whose representation space matches the query's answer can be difficult. We propose CONTLORA, which replaces stored examples with compact class statistics for adapter selection and classification. Gaussian class models in a frozen representation select LoRA adapters, while accumulated feature moments exactly recover a class-balanced ridge classifier for fixed training features. Trained without retaining images or feature vectors, CONTLORA reaches 88.55% accuracy on 20-task CIFAR-100 and 86.99% on CUB-200. Across three benchmarks in the matched component study, its mean final accuracy differs from an independently trained stored-feature counterpart by at most 0.07 percentage points. Ablations show that improved task coverage need not improve classification and adapter composition also matters. On held-out classes, competitor-centered likelihood scores improve novelty AUROC over raw likelihood without altering routing ranks. These results support statistical memory as an alternative to example-retention approaches in the evaluated settings, while identifying task ambiguity as an ongoing limitation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CONTLORA，用冻结表示中的紧凑类别统计与高斯类模型选择 LoRA 适配器，并以累积特征矩精确恢复类平衡岭分类器，在不保存样例的情况下完成持续图像分类。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按表示空间匹配度路由和组合适配器、并用似然分数判别新类的做法，可能为 LVR 的工作区选择、模块路由与证据筛选提供方法线索，但未涉及多模态推理，可迁移性需核查。
